## Welcome!

Thank you for your interest in Tools for Automated Data Analysis (TADA).
TADA is an open-source tool set built in the R programming language.
This [RMarkdown](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/) document walks
users through how to download the EPATADA R package from GitHub, access
and parameterize several important functions, and create basic
visualizations with a sample data set.

**Note: EPATADA is still under development. New functionality is added
weekly, and sometimes we need to make bug fixes in response to tester
and user feedback. We appreciate your feedback, patience, and interest
in these helpful tools.**

**If you are interested in contributing to EPATADA development, more
information is available at:**

[**Contributing**](https://usepa.github.io/EPATADA/articles/CONTRIBUTING.html)

**We welcome collaboration with external partners.**

## Install and load packages

First, install and load the remotes package specifying the repo. This is
needed before installing EPATADA because it is only available on GitHub.

```{r install_remotes, results = 'hide', eval = F}
install.packages("remotes",
  repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org"
)
library(remotes)
```

Next, install and load the EPATADA R Package using the remotes package.
Dependency packages will also be downloaded automatically from CRAN. You
may be prompted in the console to update dependencies that have more
recent versions available. If you see this prompt, it is recommended to
update all of them (enter 1 into the console).

```{r install_TADA_dev, eval = T, include = F}
# helps with development (knit and checks), this chunk should not appear on website
remotes::install_github("USEPA/EPATADA",
  ref = "Create-Module-3-AURef",
  dependencies = TRUE
)
```

```{r install_TADA, eval = F, results = 'hide'}
remotes::install_github("USEPA/EPATADA",
  ref = "develop",
  dependencies = TRUE
)
```

Finally, use the **library()** function to load the EPATADA R Package
into your R session.

```{r library, results = 'hide'}
library(EPATADA)
```

## Help pages

All TADA R package functions have their own individual help pages,
listed on the [Function
reference](https://usepa.github.io/EPATADA/reference/index.html) page on
the GitHub site. Users can also access the help page for a given
function in R or RStudio using the following format (example below):
`?[name of TADA function]`

```{r help_pages, eval = F}
# Access help page for TADA_DataRetrieval
?TADA_DataRetrieval
```

## Module 3 Functions in TADA

Disclaimer: The EPATADA Module 3 functions were designed to: (1) assist
users with associating Water Quality Portal monitoring locations with
assessment units and designated uses from ATTAINS and (2) compare Water
Quality Portal results with numeric water quality criteria. EPATADA
functions do not constitute current EPA policy or regulatory
requirements. Organizations may choose to use EPATADA as a a tool in
their decision making processes. Use of EPATADA is not required.

## Introduction

Please see "TADA Module 3a: Associating WQP Characteristics with
Applicable ATTAINS Parameters and Uses" on information on creating the
necessary crosswalk tables prior to this step.

Once a user has completed the necessary crosswalk tables, they can
proceed to defining their organization's criteria and methods for a
parameter and use. The EPA304a standards, if a user has chosen to
include, will be auto-populated. Users are able to modify these methods
as desire.

We will start off by loading in the paramRef and useParamRef crosswalk
reference files that were created during the TADA module 3a vignette.

```{r}
Data_NCTC <- Data_HUC8_02070004_Mod1Output

NCTC_ParamRef <- TADA_CreateParamRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  org_id = c("WVDEP"), 
  # excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

ParamRef <- dplyr::mutate(NCTC_ParamRef, ATTAINS.ParameterName = dplyr::case_when(
  grepl("PH", TADA.ComparableDataIdentifier) ~ "PH",
  grepl("ZINC", TADA.ComparableDataIdentifier) ~ "ZINC",
  grepl("NITRATE", TADA.ComparableDataIdentifier) ~ "NITROGEN, TOTAL"
))

NCTC_ParamRef_Final <- TADA_CreateParamRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  org_id = c("WVDEP"),
  paramRef = ParamRef,
  excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)
# Now, run TADA_CreateUseParamRef once you have completed filling out your paramRef from TADA_CreateParamRef.
NCTC_UseParamRef <- TADA_CreateUseParamRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  org_id = c("WVDEP"),
  paramRef = NCTC_ParamRef_Final,
  # excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

add_data <- data.frame("organization_identifier" = "WVDEP", "ATTAINS.ParameterName" = rep("NITROGEN, TOTAL", 3), "use_name" = c(
  "Agriculture and Wildlife", "Water Contact Recreation: Recreation",
  "Warm Water Fishery"
))

# The output of this will not reflect changes to the ATTAINS.FlagUseName column. To do so, we need to re run TADA_CreateUseParamRef() with UseParamRef = UseParamRef as an argument.
UseParamRef_Modified <- NCTC_UseParamRef %>%
  dplyr::left_join(add_data, by = c("organization_identifier", "ATTAINS.ParameterName"), keep = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(use_name = dplyr::coalesce(use_name.x, use_name.y)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(use_name.x, use_name.y))

# NITROGEN, TOTAL will now reflect the changes
NCTC_UseParamRef_Final <- TADA_CreateUseParamRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  paramRef = NCTC_ParamRef_Final,
  useParamRef = UseParamRef_Modified, # Edits were made to UseParamRef, updates flag column
  org_id = c("WVDEP"),
  excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)
```

# Create and Define Spatial Reference Tables

We can define your WQP data retrieval on either an assessment unit level
summary or monitoring location sites level. Please refer to EPATADA
Module 2 on more information on the geospatial functions to assist with
your assessment unit and monitoring location sites overlay.

The general workflow of running module 3 functions for CWA water quality
data analysis is shown below.

TADA_CreateParamRef requires a crosswalk between ATTAINS parameter names
and WQP characteristic names/TADA comparable data identifiers.

![Monitoring Location Summary](images/FlowChartMLModule3.jpg)

![Assessment Unit Level Summary](images/FlowChartAUModule3.jpg)

Additional resources:

-   Review function documentation by entering the following code into
    the console:
    -   ?TADA_CreateParamRef
    -   ?TADA_CreateUseParamRef
    -   ?TADA_CreateSpatialRef
        -   ?TADA_CreateUseAURef
        -   ?TADA_CreateUseWaterParamRef

### 'TADA_CreateSpatialRef()' on a ML sites Level

For our first example, let's view what the TADA_CreateSpatial Summary
output looks like.

If you are interested in only a monitoring location level summary of
your WQP data retrieval, you do not need to perform any monitoring sites
to assessment unit crosswalk table. In this scenario, you will only need
to run, in this order:

1)  TADA_CreateParamRef()
2)  TADA_CreateUseParamRef()
3)  TADA_CreateSpatialRef(): For this function, you **do not** need to
    provide the argument inputs for **useAURef** or **waterUseParamRef**

```{r}
NCTC_SpatialRef_ML <- TADA_CreateSpatialRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  org_id = "WVDEP",
  useParamRef = NCTC_UseParamRef_Final,
  # excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

TADA_TableExport(NCTC_SpatialRef_ML)
```

We can apply any unique spatial criteria on a monitoring location sites
level. This view allows us to determine whether there are certain sites
that needs a unique site-specific criteria, certain water types, or
certain combination of characteristics that have site-specific criteria.
Let's go through an example of how a user may modify this table.

```{r}
add_data_spatial_ML <- data.frame(
  MonitoringLocationTypeName = c(rep("Stream", 4)), 
  ATTAINS.ParameterName = c(rep("PH", 4)),
  ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria = c("Upper-Stream", "Lower-Stream", "Warm-Water", "Cold-water")
  )

NCTC_SpatialRef_ML_Modified <- dplyr::left_join(
  NCTC_SpatialRef_ML, add_data_spatial_ML, 
  by = c("MonitoringLocationTypeName", "ATTAINS.ParameterName"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria = dplyr::coalesce(ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria.x, ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria.y)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria.x, ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria.y))

NCTC_SpatialRef_ML_Final <- TADA_CreateSpatialRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  org_id = "WVDEP",
  useParamRef = NCTC_UseParamRef_Final,
  spatialRef = NCTC_SpatialRef_ML_Modified
  # excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

TADA_TableExport(NCTC_SpatialRef_ML_Final)
```

### 'TADA_CreateSpatialRef()' on an Assessment Unit Level

Now, if you are interested in summarizing results on an assessment unit
level, it is highly recommended to run the two helper function to run
through this step by step process on how you may review or specify
site-specific criteria prior to creating and defining your Criteria and
Methodology table for a parameter, use and water type.

First, we will got through an example of how you can utilize the results
directly from TADA_GetATTAINS() as your ML to AU crosswalk. This
crosswalk table will be named SiteAURef.

```{r}
GetATTAINSRef <- TADA_GetATTAINS(Data_NCTC, return_sf = FALSE)
sitesAURef <- GetATTAINSRef

TADA_TableExport(sitesAURef)
```

In this example, we demonstrate what your output table will look like in
TADA_CreateSpatialRef() if you decide to not run the two helper
functions: TADA_CreateUseAURef() and TADA_CreateWaterUseParamRef().

These helper functions are not required, but will help to further review
your ML to AU crosswalk (modification to AU, new AU, new WQP sites etc.)
as well as provide support in filling out site-specific criteria. In
this example, our spatial area in our TADA data frame contains WQP
observations from other states (MD, PA, VA). These observations are
flagged in the column Flag.AssessmentNote. It is up to the user to
decide if these are relevant to their assessments, and if not, they
should remove these rows. This column will also help to identify other
cases such as no ML to AU matches, no use_names associated with your AUs
and more! (Still in development)

```{r}
NCTC_SpatialRef_No_Helper <- TADA_CreateSpatialRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  org_id = "WVDEP",
  sitesAURef = sitesAURef,
  useParamRef = NCTC_UseParamRef_Final,
  # useAURef = NCTC_UseAURef,
  # waterUseParamRef = NCTC_WaterUseParamRef_Final,
  excel = FALSE
  # excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

TADA_TableExport(NCTC_SpatialRef_No_Helper)
```

Now, lets run through an example with the helper functions. We must run
these helper functions in order. First, we will run
TADA_CreateUseAURef(). This will use the rExpertQuery data query pull of
ATTAINS national extracts to pull in prior use_names associated with
your assessment units. This helper function is helpful in cases in which
a user has new AU or modified AU that are not found in prior ATTAINS
cycles. In this case, it is important that users define these use names
associated with those AUs as TADA will be unable to tell what use names
are appropriate and will require your review.

We will add examples with new AU and use names example.

```{r}
NCTC_UseAURef <- TADA_CreateUseAURef(
  Data_NCTC,
  sitesAURef = sitesAURef,
  org_id = "WVDEP",
  excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

add_new_AU <- data.frame(
  organization_identifier = c(rep("WVDEP", 4)),
  waterType = c(rep("RIVER", 4)),
  ATTAINS.assessmentunitidentifier = c(rep("NEW_WV_AU1", 2), rep("NEW_WV_AU1", 2)),
  ATTAINS.assessmentunitname = c(rep("EXAMPLE_WV_AU1", 2), rep("EXAMPLE_WV_AU1", 2)),
  use_name = c(rep("Public Water Supply", 3), "Warm Water Fishery"),
  # lon = c(rep(-78.20000, 2), rep(-78.10000, 2)),
  # lat = c(rep(39.64000, 2), rep(39.65000, 2)),
  TADA.AssessmentUnitStatus = c(rep("New", 4))
)

# add_new_AU <- sf::st_as_sf(x = add_new_AU, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)


NCTC_UseAURef_Modified <- NCTC_UseAURef %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(add_new_AU) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(!ATTAINS.assessmentunitidentifier %in% "WV-PL-20_03")


# The functions are meant to be reusable and flag any rows accordingly to show any changes that may have occurred since your last Assessment cycle. To re-use your useAURef = NCTC_UseAURef_Modified you must provide the sitesAURef.
NCTC_UseAURef_Final <- TADA_CreateUseAURef(
  Data_NCTC,
  sitesAURef = sitesAURef,
  useAURef = NCTC_UseAURef_Modified, # validates your table
  org_id = "WVDEP",
  excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

TADA_TableExport(NCTC_UseAURef_Final)
```

Now we will run TADA_CreateWaterUseParamRef(). This requires the output
from TADA_CreateUseAURef() as an argument input.

```{r}
NCTC_WaterUseParamRef <- TADA_CreateWaterUseParamRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  useAURef = NCTC_UseAURef_Final,
  useParamRef = NCTC_UseParamRef_Final,
  org_id = "WVDEP",
  excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

add_data_WaterUse <- data.frame(
  waterType = c(rep("STREAM/CREEK/RIVER", 4)),
  ATTAINS.ParameterName = c(rep("PH", 4)),
  ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria = c("Upper-Stream", "Lower-Stream", "Warm-Water", "Cold-water")
  )

NCTC_WaterUseParamRef_Modified <- NCTC_WaterUseParamRef %>% 
  tidyr::uncount(2) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria = rep(c("Y","N"), times =21))
  

NCTC_WaterUseParamRef_Modified <- dplyr::left_join(NCTC_WaterUseParamRef, add_data_WaterUse, by = c("waterType", "ATTAINS.ParameterName"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria = dplyr::coalesce(ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria.x, ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria.y)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria.x, ApplyUniqueSpatialCriteria.y))

TADA_TableExport(NCTC_WaterUseParamRef_Modified)

NCTC_WaterUseParamRef_Final <- TADA_CreateWaterUseParamRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  useAURef = NCTC_UseAURef_Final,
  useParamRef = NCTC_UseParamRef_Final,
  waterUseParamRef = NCTC_WaterUseParamRef_Modified, #validates the entries of your completed table
  org_id = "WVDEP",
  excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)
```

Now that we have done our step by step review, we will use our two
helper functions to create our spatial ref table on an AU level. We will
review the table to make any final updates as we feel is needed. Let's
filter our flags by only "Pass" as we have determined these additional
WQP sites fall outside of our spatial area of interest.

```{r}
NCTC_SpatialRef_AU <- TADA_CreateSpatialRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  org_id = "WVDEP",
  sitesAURef = sitesAURef,
  useAURef = NCTC_UseAURef_Final,
  useParamRef = NCTC_UseParamRef_Final,
  waterUseParamRef = NCTC_WaterUseParamRef_Final,
  excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

NCTC_SpatialRef_AU_Final <- dplyr::filter(NCTC_SpatialRef_AU, Flag.AssessmentNote == "Pass")

TADA_TableExport(NCTC_SpatialRef_AU_Final)
```

As another case if a user is interested, if a user has only filled out
TADA_CreateUseAURef() and want to skip running
TADA_CreateWaterUseParamRef, what will our Spatial Ref table look like?
In this scenario, we will assume user does not need to modify the
TADA_CreateWaterUseParamRef() and run it in TADA_CreateSpatialRef().

```{r}
NCTC_SpatialRef_AU_No_WaterUseParam <- TADA_CreateSpatialRef(
  Data_NCTC,
  org_id = "WVDEP",
  sitesAURef = sitesAURef,
  useAURef = NCTC_UseAURef_Final,
  useParamRef = NCTC_UseParamRef_Final,
  # waterUseParamRef = NCTC_WaterUseParamRef_Final,
  excel = FALSE
  # excel = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE
)

TADA_TableExport(NCTC_SpatialRef_AU_No_WaterUseParam)
```
